name: Vitamin K
short: Interacts with warfarin: changes in vitamin K intake alter anticoagulant control (INR). A review found multivitamins contain enough vitamin K1 to change coagulation measures.
text: Vitamin K is an essential co-factor for making several clotting factors, and oral anticoagulants such as warfarin act by inhibiting enzymes involved in vitamin K metabolism, so changes in vitamin K intake can alter anticoagulant control. A review reported that intakes above 250 micrograms a day decreased warfarin sensitivity, that each 100-microgram increase in intake was estimated to lower the INR by 0.2, and that over-the-counter multivitamin supplements contain enough vitamin K1 to significantly alter coagulation measures; it judged the interaction clinically relevant. In a Cochrane review of two small trials (100 participants) in which low-dose vitamin K was added to warfarin, neither trial reported thromboembolic events, haemorrhage or death from the added vitamin K.
